extracted.intended_audience: current undergraduates interested in joining the AEI Collegiate Network / prospective applicants to AEI student programs
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and expectations for current undergraduates seeking membership in the American Enterprise Institute (AEI) Collegiate Network, including eligibility, application materials, member activities, and benefits. The page describes program mission, typical events (reading groups, summits), and what membership entails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — current undergraduates
rubrics_metrics.description: The AEI Collegiate Network is 'an intellectual home for current undergraduates' and targets students on campuses around the nation and world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership is specifically for current undergraduate students; the program is aimed at the next generation of leaders in public policy, media, business, academia, law, and other fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials — updated resume and statement of intent
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief online application 'consists of an updated resume and a statement of intent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for the 2025-2026 academic year are accepted on a rolling basis. If applicants have questions, contact [email protected]. There is an 'Apply Now' link on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership mission and behavioral expectations — substantive dialogue, civil debate, free inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: AEI's mission for the Collegiate Network is to 'improve intellectual discourse on public policy on college campuses' by 'empowering individuals to engage in substantive dialogue and civil debate' and by 'fostering connections' among public‑spirited student leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members are expected to 'join a network of peers committed to civil debate and free inquiry' and to 'model a competition of ideas' on their campuses and beyond; these norms are central to participation and programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member activities — host scholars, lead reading groups, attend summits and trainings
rubrics_metrics.description: Students are offered opportunities including 'hosting AEI scholars and other nationally renowned leaders on campus for lectures, panels, and roundtable discussions,' 'leading reading groups with other students on-campus and online,' and 'attending exclusive public policy summits and conferences at AEI’s headquarters in Washington, DC and at partner campuses across the country.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These listed activities define active participation expectations and typical member engagement formats (on-campus events, online reading groups, AEI-hosted summits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summit participation — Fall Summit (fully-funded at DC HQ) and Spring Summit (partner campus for graduating seniors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year AEI hosts a Collegiate Network Fall Summit at its Washington, DC headquarters (described as 'fully-funded') for policy keynotes, panels, and student program trainings. The Collegiate Network Spring Summit gathers graduating seniors at a partner university campus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fall Summit is positioned as a fully-funded flagship event to equip students for engagement and collaboration; the Spring Summit focuses on graduating seniors and topical discussions (examples: free expression, civil discourse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading group leadership — select readings and facilitate discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Members lead reading groups on-campus and online; the page gives examples of past readings and hosting campuses (e.g., Pepperdine reading Christine Rosen's The Extinction of Experience; Harvard reading The Politically Incorrect Guide to The Supreme Court; St. Andrews reading American Covenant by Yuval Levin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leading a reading group implies choosing substantive, policy‑oriented texts and facilitating discussion among peers, both in-person and online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional development and networking outcomes — exposure to AEI scholars and career/academic advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership 'provides students with educational and professional opportunities' including exposure to AEI scholarship and scholars, and networking with peers nationwide. Alumni outcomes cited: attending top graduate schools, working on Capitol Hill and at DC think tanks, and being published in leading newspapers and magazines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program markets these outcomes as measures of benefit and expected return on participation; prospective members can consider these as implicit success criteria for participation.
